main_text.p: collocatione artificiosa & varia est cogitandum. Sunt autem argumenta hic adhibenda Argumenta commendationum probantia.da primum commedatio-δεικτικά[?] docentia & probantia; num probanti-eaque sumenda vel à rei ipsius, qua de agitur, honestate & æquitate: vel facili & tia.δυνάτῳ: vel utili, & gratitudinis eorū quos commendamus pollicitatione: vel eiusdem antè nobis præstitis beneficiis: vel nostro aliorumque exemplo: vel testimonio, iudicio, authoritate magnorum virorum: vel intercessione atq; precibꝰ amicorum.

Deinde ad πάθη animorum motus quod attinet, reperiuntur hic spes, & metus, odium, & amor: maximè verò misericordia, quæ excitanda erga pauperes, exules, adversa fortuna oppressos: ita quidem, ut ostendatur eandem quoq; aliis, maximè verò iis ad quos scribimus metuendam esse. παθητικὰ, mo-venita argu-menta.

Tum & illi qui commendationes instituę recupiunt, eorum ad quos scribunt fibi & amicis, quos commendant conciliare animos necesse habent: aut laude eorum quibus literas dant commendatitias: sine tamen κολακείᾳ adulatione, & commendatione nimis aperta, aut exaggerata: aut modesta atq; verecunda excusatione, & expositione causarum institutæ commendationis: aut animi grati perpetuæque me-

page.notes: Greek words (δεικτικά, δυνάτῳ, πάθη, κολακείᾳ) and the Greek marginal notes are read from a small, slightly blurred scan; the first Greek word and the marginal Greek notes are doubtful. The marginal word "venita" and "liantia" are uncertain; the margin reads roughly "Ventila argumenta" and "Conciliantia argumenta". "instituę" and "ostendatur" are uncertain because the first letter is partly cut off. The bottom signature and the page number mark were hard to read and are not transcribed. Running head read as COMMENDATITIIS. The bottom-of-page footnote and the line-end hyphenation of "adhibenda" have no visible hyphen.
